subject: Prepay options and ramp schedule — 12/24 month proposals for BlueWave
messages:
From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Amit Shah <amit@bluewave.ai>, Nora Li <nora@bluewave.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Feb 2026 15:23:00 -0500
Subject: Prepay options and ramp schedule — 12/24 month proposals for BlueWave

Hi Amit / Nora,

Thanks again for the time on today’s call. Per our discussion, I’m attaching two prepay structures that are common for early-stage customers and designed to give you predictable unit economics while accommodating an initial ramp: a 12-month prepay and a 24-month prepay. High-level summary here so it’s easy to share with your CFO/procure team: 

- 12-month prepay (Option A): $200,000 prepayment for usage credits — equivalent to ~15% off list token pricing for your expected workload profile. Optional 3-month ramp schedule where minimum billing is staged.
- 24-month prepay (Option B): $380,000 prepayment — ~22% effective discount, with a built-in annual smooth.
- Startup onboarding concession: $50,000 one-time usage credit applied to Q1 to help cover initial evaluation and dev traffic.
- Ramp mechanics: months 1–3 partial minimums (25–50% depending on smoothing), months 4+ bill to committed monthly baseline. Unused prepay credits limited-carry for first 90 days; after that credits are applied to usage only.
- Flex: Option to convert to Dedicated (reserved capacity) with 6 months’ notice and a migration surcharge; pricing to be modeled at conversion time.

I’ve attached a draft term sheet and the pricing worksheet. Please flag the items you want us to tighten (payment terms, carryover, SLA language). If this looks sensible I can loop in Sales Ops / Finance to produce a redline for procurement.

Attachments: RW-BlueWave-Prepay-Termsheet-v1.pdf; RW-BlueWave-Pricing-worksheet.xlsx

Next steps suggested: 1) Confirm target option (12 vs 24) 2) Confirm desired ramp softness (aggressive vs smooth) 3) Procure/finance contact for PO and payment terms.

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0192

From: Nora Li <nora@bluewave.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Prepay options and ramp schedule — 12/24 month proposals for BlueWave

Thanks, Sean — useful summary. A few clarifying questions before we take to finance: 

1) Ramp: The carryover language — you said "limited-carry for first 90 days". Can you confirm exactly how much of unused credits can roll into month 4? We need to avoid losing credits from a slow first-quarter product launch.
2) Payment terms: Do you offer Net-30 or Net-45 for startups? Our standard is Net-30 but our seed round bank covenants sometimes push to Net-45.
3) SLA credits: can SLA credit language be included in the term sheet? We need at least a 99.9% target and a defined credit schedule.

Putting our procurement alias on copy so they can coordinate: procure@bluewave.ai

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:08:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Prepay options and ramp schedule — 12/24 month proposals for BlueWave

Nora — great questions. Quick answers below; I’ve asked Marissa (Sales Ops) and Dev (Finance) to weigh in on final payment/legal language.

1) Carryover: we can allow up to 100% of unused credits from months 1–3 to carry into month 4 but only for the first 90 days post-purchase. After 90 days unused credits are forfeited. Practically, that means any credits not consumed in months 1–3 can be used against months 4–6. We can make an exception for documented launch delays with advance notice.

2) Payment terms: standard for early-stage customers is Net-30. For startups we can offer Net-45 on a case-by-case basis with a small processing fee (0.5% of invoice) if Finance signs off. Marissa, Dev — can you confirm?

3) SLA credits: we’ll include a 99.9% availability target in the term sheet with a tiered credit schedule (0.1%–0.5% credits based on month-level downtime). I’ll add the explicit section to the redline.

I’m attaching an updated pricing worksheet that shows effective per-token costs under Option A and B and an example ramp-month cashflow. If you prefer an alternate smoothing (e.g., 50% of baseline in month 1 then linear catch-up), we can model that too.

Attachments: RW-BlueWave-Pricing-worksheet.xlsx

Best,
Sean

Appreciate the clarity, Sean. A couple of follow-ups from finance/exec: 

- Can you provide a final bill schedule for Option A (12-month) showing month-by-month invoicing for both the aggressive ramp and the smooth ramp? We need this for our cap table & cashflow modeling.
- SLA: please add the credit schedule to the term sheet. We’ll expect that the credit is deducted from future invoices and not applied as a separate cash payment.
- Payment terms: we prefer Net-45 if possible; is Redwood comfortable with Net-45 for the first invoice and Net-30 afterwards?

If you can get a redlined term sheet with the above and a firm month-by-month invoice example, I can fast-track to our CEO and procurement.

Thanks,
Amit Shah
CEO | BlueWave Analytics
amit@bluewave.ai

Hi Amit / Nora — looping in Sales Ops / Finance here with concrete redlines. Attached is a redlined term sheet (RW-BlueWave-Termsheet-redline-v2.pdf) and an updated pricing spreadsheet that includes both the aggressive ramp and the smooth ramp invoice examples. Highlights of what we can commit to for an early-stage partner: 

- Payment terms: Net-45 on the first invoice, Net-30 thereafter (no processing fee for your stage).
- Ramp smoothing: offer a smoothing option where months 1–3 are billed at 50% of baseline, with a linear catch-up spread across months 4–6. This removes the front-loaded pressure on product launch months.
- Carryover: permit 100% carryover of months 1–3 into months 4–6 for documented launches (email notice required pre-day-1).
- Startup concession: apply the $50k onboarding credit to the first invoice line and it will be consumed before other credits.
- SLA credits: included as invoice offsets per the schedule in the redline.

We’ve kept the headline economics intact: $200k prepay for 12 months (Option A) at ~15% effective discount; $380k for 24 months (Option B) at ~22%. If this matches what you need, I’ll prepare the final DocuSign package and a sample invoice for your accounting team.

Attachments: RW-BlueWave-Termsheet-redline-v2.pdf; RW-BlueWave-Pricing-worksheet.xlsx

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Head of Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
